facts.meaning: The automatic answer contains intent and text, without an echoed question field.
Text is not emitted until a complete answer intent has been decoded. A text-first answer cannot emit until the subsequent intent field arrives.
Once answer intent is available, decoded nonempty text prefixes are emitted incrementally; closing the whole JSON object is not required.
The accumulated JSON prefix is reparsed on each chunk; work can grow with cumulative output and chunk count. This is a source-level cost, not a measured tail attribution.
Decoder execution happens before the callback-duration timer; small callback times do not measure decoder cost.
FirstAgentDelta is marked in dispatch, before filtering blocked old agent items and before JSON gating. It is not reset per final answer frame.
The existing passing framing test checks incremental exact text and split escapes and withholding a text-first ignore reply; it is not a latency benchmark.

measurementLimitations: Current recordings do not preserve raw agent JSON chunks or final-frame first raw delta timestamps. Actual field order and decoder execution time cannot be reconstructed reliably.
The measured same-response confirmation-to-send and send-to-reader waits occur before decoding the final response. JSON gating cannot explain those intervals.
Consumer-to-retained-delta includes backend output arrival, decoding, frame/context filtering and native processing; it is not isolated model compute time.
No production behavior, prompts, or backend routing changed. No new build or expensive decoder benchmark during measured capture.
